udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
Contract errors.

Deliberately renumbered for the v1 interface so the error space is disjoint
from the legacy (pre-1.0) contract's 1-9 range. A client decoding an error
code < 100 is talking to a legacy wallet.

Ranges:
- 100-109: signer storage / management
- 110-119: auth (`__check_auth`)
- 120-129: WebAuthn (secp256r1) verification
- 130-139: Secp256r1 signer binding
udt_error_enum_v0.name: Error

cases.doc: The requested signer does not exist on this smart wallet.
cases.name: SignerNotFound

cases.doc: `add_signer` was called with a signer key that already exists.
cases.name: SignerAlreadyExists

cases.doc: The signer's expiration timestamp is in the past.
cases.name: SignerExpired

cases.doc:
The operation would remove \xe2\x80\x94 or demote via `update_signer` \xe2\x80\x94 the
wallet's LAST durable admin signer: a signer stored `Persistent`,
non-expiring (`SignerExpiration(None)`), and independently
admin-capable \xe2\x80\x94 either unlimited (`SignerLimits(None)`) or holding a
limits entry for the wallet's own address with no required co-signers
(`None` or an empty list). With zero such signers no `add_signer` or
`upgrade` could ever be authorized again, permanently locking the
wallet on an immutable network, so the transition is rejected.
To retire the last admin signer, add (or promote) a replacement
durable admin signer first.

Case this guard CANNOT catch (statically undecidable): a POLICY
signer with an admin-shaped grant counts as an admin even if its
`policy__` rejects every request. If such a policy is your only
remaining admin, the wallet's admin surface is unrecoverable even
though the signer still exists. Keep a non-policy admin (or a second
admin) at all times.
cases.name: LastAdminSigner

cases.doc:
The operation would leave the wallet without any DURABLE signer \xe2\x80\x94 one
stored `Persistent` with `SignerExpiration(None)`, any limits. Fired
by `remove_signer` (removing the last durable signer), `update_signer`
(demoting it to `Temporary` storage or to an expiring value), and
`__constructor` (the wallet's first signer must be durable).
Non-durable signers can evict or expire with NO contract
call, so only a durable signer guarantees the wallet always keeps at
least one live signer; with zero live signers nothing \xe2\x80\x94 not even
`add_signer` \xe2\x80\x94 can ever be authorized again. This is the
classification-independent backstop beneath `LastAdminSigner`. To
retire the last durable signer, add a durable replacement first.
cases.name: LastSigner

cases.doc: No signer in the signatures map is permitted to authorize one of the\nrequested auth contexts.
cases.name: MissingContext

cases.doc: A signature's variant does not match the stored signer it claims to be\nfor (e.g. an Ed25519 signature submitted for a Policy signer key).
cases.name: SignatureKeyValueMismatch

cases.doc: clientDataJSON exceeds the 1024 byte parse buffer.
cases.name: ClientDataJsonTooLarge

cases.doc: clientDataJSON is not parseable JSON (or is missing required fields).
cases.name: ClientDataJsonParseError

cases.doc: The challenge in clientDataJSON does not match the base64url-encoded\nsignature payload. This binds the WebAuthn assertion to the Soroban\nauthorization entry and MUST NOT be weakened.
cases.name: ClientDataJsonChallengeIncorrect

cases.doc: authenticatorData is shorter than the WebAuthn minimum of 37 bytes\n(rpIdHash 32 + flags 1 + signCount 4).
cases.name: InvalidAuthenticatorData

cases.doc:
The authenticator did not set the User Present (UP) flag.

UP-only is the deliberate default. Requiring UP keeps
silent, non-interactive assertions out while staying compatible with
authenticators that cannot do User Verification (UV \xe2\x80\x94 biometric/PIN).
UV is therefore NOT required by this contract. A deployment that wants
UV-required assertions should enforce it at the client/relayer layer,
or via a future per-signer flag (which would be a signer-model change,
not a change to this check); the contract cannot upgrade UP-only
signers to UV-required retroactively without such a flag.
cases.name: UserPresenceRequired

cases.doc:
authenticatorData exceeds the 1024 byte cap (symmetric with
`ClientDataJsonTooLarge`). Real assertions are ~37 bytes; the cap
rejects oversized input BEFORE it is hashed, since this path is
reachable without a valid signature.
cases.name: AuthenticatorDataTooLarge

cases.doc: A Secp256r1 signer was supplied without its binding proof. Passkeys\nenter a wallet only through `__constructor` (GENESIS proof) or\n`add_secp256r1` (ADD proof) \xe2\x80\x94 never through the generic `add_signer`.
cases.name: BindingProofRequired

cases.doc: A binding proof was supplied for a signer that is not Secp256r1.
cases.name: BindingProofUnexpected

cases.doc:
`update_signer` may not change a Secp256r1 signer's public key: the
binding proof commits to it. Remove the signer and re-add it with a
fresh proof through `add_secp256r1` instead.

Code 132 is retired with `bind_secp256r1`; 134 with its
already-bound guard. Neither is reused.
cases.name: BindingPublicKeyImmutable

udt_union_v0.doc: Full signer description used by `__constructor`, `add_signer` and\n`update_signer`.
udt_union_v0.name: Signer

udt_union_v0.doc: A signature entry in the signatures map. `Policy` carries no signature\nmaterial: inclusion of the policy key authorizes an on-chain `policy__`\ncheck instead.
udt_union_v0.name: Signature

udt_union_v0.doc: Storage key identifying a signer. Secp256r1 carries the WebAuthn\ncredential id (`keyId`).
udt_union_v0.name: SignerKey

udt_union_v0.doc: Stored signer value. Secp256r1 carries the SEC-1 uncompressed public key.
udt_union_v0.name: SignerVal

udt_union_v0.doc:
Storage keys for wallet entries that are NOT signer entries. Every variant
name here must stay distinct from every `SignerKey` variant name: a
`#[contracttype]` enum encodes as `[Symbol(variant), fields\xe2\x80\xa6]` with no
type name, so a shared variant name would collide in contract storage.
udt_union_v0.name: BindingKey

tuple_v0.doc: A `Secp256r1BindingRecord`, keyed by the signer's credential id and\nstored in the same durability as the signer entry.
tuple_v0.name: Secp256r1Binding

udt_struct_v0.doc: The `__check_auth` signature object: a map of signer keys to signatures.\nMap ordering is the host's ScVal ordering. EVERY entry must verify (pass\n2 of `__check_auth`) \xe2\x80\x94 include only signatures that are needed.
udt_struct_v0.name: Signatures

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Authorization limits for a signer.

- `None`: unlimited.
- `Some(empty map)`: no independent authority.
- `Some({address -> None})`: any invocation of `address`.
- `Some({address -> Some([keys])})`: any invocation of `address` only when
every listed key also approves.

A required key approves independently of its own limits. A required
non-policy key must appear in the signatures map and pass full verification.
A required policy need not appear there, but it must remain stored and
unexpired. It must also approve through `policy__`. Removing it revokes all
dependent signers.

Limited signers cannot authorize `CreateContract*`. A limited cryptographic
signer can remove itself without satisfying its limits. A policy signature
always calls `policy__`, including during self-removal. A limit for the
wallet address grants access to the wallet administration functions.
udt_struct_v0.name: SignerLimits

udt_union_v0.doc: Which durability a signer entry is stored under. At most one entry exists\nper signer key; lookups check Temporary before Persistent.
udt_union_v0.name: SignerStorage

udt_union_v0.doc:
What a binding proof authorizes. Carried in the challenge preimage AND
reflected in the domain separator, so the two proof spaces are disjoint
twice over: a GENESIS proof can never be replayed into `add_secp256r1`,
and an ADD proof can never seed a constructor.
udt_union_v0.name: BindingPurpose

void_v0.doc: The wallet's first signer, supplied to `__constructor`.
void_v0.name: Genesis

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Optional expiration for a signer as a UNIX timestamp in seconds, INCLUSIVE:
the signer is valid while `ledger timestamp <= expiration` and expired once
`ledger timestamp > expiration`. `None` never expires.

v1 breaking change: this was a ledger sequence number pre-1.0. Timestamps
don't drift with changes to ledger close time (e.g. CAP-0070 dynamic
timing), which ledger-sequence expirations did.
udt_struct_v0.name: SignerExpiration

udt_struct_v0.doc: A WebAuthn assertion over the Soroban authorization payload. The signed\nmessage is `authenticator_data || sha256(client_data_json)` and the\npayload binding lives in clientDataJSON's `challenge` field.
udt_struct_v0.name: Secp256r1Signature

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A passkey's binding to this wallet: the exact signer it consented to, the
purpose that consent was given for, and the WebAuthn assertion it produced
over the corresponding challenge.

Stored under `BindingKey::Secp256r1Binding(key_id)` in the signer's
durability; written only by `__constructor` and `add_secp256r1`, each of
which verifies `proof` first.

`signer` is the ORIGINAL value and is never rewritten: `update_signer` may
reshape the live signer's mutable policy fields, and the record continues
to attest what was actually signed. Its key id and public key must still
equal the live signer's \xe2\x80\x94 `get_secp256r1_binding` enforces that on read.
udt_struct_v0.name: Secp256r1BindingRecord

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The preimage of a Secp256r1 binding challenge. The challenge is
`sha256(XDR(payload))` \xe2\x80\x94 see `binding::secp256r1_binding_challenge`.

The proof commits to the FULL original `Signer`, not just its key
material. A holder consents to one exact signer value on one wallet on one
network for one purpose, so a stolen pending proof cannot be re-aimed at a
different shape \xe2\x80\x94 in particular it cannot be used to seat the holder's
passkey with limits that leave the wallet with no admin.
udt_struct_v0.name: Secp256r1BindingPayload

fields.doc: `env.ledger().network_id()` of the network the wallet lives on.
fields.name: network_id

fields.doc: Which entry point the proof authorizes.
fields.name: purpose

fields.doc: The complete signer value the holder consented to, including\nexpiration, limits, and storage durability.
fields.name: signer

event_v0.doc:
The contract's wasm was replaced via `upgrade`. `old_hash` is `None` on a
wallet's first-ever upgrade: the host exposes no way for a contract to
read its own executable hash, so the wallet caches the hash in instance
storage at each upgrade and the genesis hash is unknowable in-contract.
event_v0.name: Upgraded

event_v0.doc: A signer was removed via `remove_signer`. `storage` is the durability the\nentry was removed from.
event_v0.name: SignerRemoved

event_v0.doc: An existing signer was modified via `update_signer`.
event_v0.name: SignerUpdated
